analysis:
The only production change is SSDPrefixCachePolicy.swift line 245, which raises writeQueueMaxJobs from 2 to 6 and expands the doc comment (lines 233-244). The other files are tests and a test fixture (startDonation helper, SSDCheckpointFleetWritePriorityTests, SSDHybridCheckpointStoreTests) and carry no production behavior.

Security relevance is T-041 and the SSD at-rest tier. The constant bounds the buffered donation jobs behind the serial write-behind consumer. It does not change the TTL (still 30 min, max equals default, env can only shorten, lines 36-37), the HMAC lookup-tag derivation, the DBK3 crypto, the account/salt scoping, the daily write cap (line 53), the low-disk floor (line 205), or the queued-byte cap (writeQueueMaxBytes, 512 MiB, line 252). Attention jobs must still fit that byte cap, so host-RAM exposure from queued plaintext KV stays bounded. A deeper queue means at most 6 pending jobs instead of 2. The comment states that complete-checkpoint jobs hold only donor state and I/O scratch charged to the admission or process memory ledger, and that the donor stream end and state release are delayed under write backlog. That is a latency and memory-hold trade-off, which I did not verify in the SSDHybridCheckpointStore or engine code, since neither was supplied. The residual risk is transient plaintext KV sitting longer in process memory and slightly higher disk write volume. Write volume is still bounded by the rolling-day cap and the per-write admission checks, which the updated tests confirm cover the writer path. Bounded queue growth does not open a new disclosure channel for co-tenants or disk observers.

The tests confirm a refusal with the writeQueueFull outcome at 6 pending jobs and a settle-time admission race fix, but the store implementation (pipeline acceptedCount, the gate) was not supplied. The following should be checked in integration: that the complete-checkpoint store really enforces the 6-job bound including the job being written, and that donor memory remains charged to the ledger while queued. No concrete regression is identified.
